NOTICE AND AGENDA
  FOR SPECIAL MEETING

  CITY COUNCIL

  December 17, 2019

  NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor of the City of Norwalk has called a special
  meeting of the City Council beginning at 6:00 p.m. on December 17, 2019 in the City Council
  Chambers, Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard. The agenda for the special meeting is
  as follows:

  (Members of the public are entitled to speak only on the item listed. Please fill out a speaker card
  and turn it in to the Sergeant at Arms before the meeting commences.)

  CALL TO ORDER  Mayor Rios

  ROLL CALL  City Clerk

  CONSENT

  REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR A CARNIVAL - Staff recommends City
  Council approve the carnival requested by the Norwalk Float Foundation for the dates of
  Thursday, February 13 through Sunday, February 16, 2020 and waive the security deposit and
  fees as requested consistent with past practice.  920-01-02

  Dated this 16th day of December 2019.

  I, Theresa Devoy, City Clerk, hereby certify that the foregoing notice of special meeting was posted at City
  Hall not less than 24-hours before the start of the meeting and delivered to each member of the Norwalk
  City Council and to the following newspapers: Herald American, Cerritos Community News, Norwalk
  Patriot, and Whittier Daily News, all on the 16th day of December 2019.

  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s Department.

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the City Council on any matter listed on the agenda.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
documents in the agenda packet, can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
Notification of at least 12 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.
   City Council Agenda Report
  December 17, 2019

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Gabriela Garcia, Management Analyst

SUBJECT: REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR A CARNIVAL

Background:

The Norwalk Float Foundation has submitted correspondence to the City requesting use
of the Civic Center Lawn for a fundraising carnival from Thursday, February 13 through
Sunday, February 16, 2020. Requested dates include setup, carnival operation, and
cleanup.

The City will be hosting a Waste Collection Event on Saturday, February 15, but the event
will end before the carnival start time. The Norwalk Float Foundation has indicated they
will provide trash disposal, portable restrooms, and sinks for the carnival. They will also
assume responsibility for providing security during the carnival operating days and for
cleaning both the City Hall and Library parking lots.

Carnival Rules:

Staff enforces all carnival rules including requirements for payment of carnival fees, clean
up deposits, equipment arrival and departure times, screening of vehicles and equipment,
and supervision of carnival operations by sponsoring organizations.

Applicant Carnival Expenses:

The following summarizes the estimated costs incurred by carnival organizer:

  Carnival and special event permit fees  $ 465
  Business license fees ($100/day x 4 days)  $ 400
  Electrical and safety permit fees  $ 658
  Total Applicant Carnival Expenses  $1,523
 City Council  December 17, 2019
Use of Civic Center Lawn – Carnival  Page No. 2

In addition, the applicant is required to pay a $1,000 security deposit. The applicant is
requesting a waiver of the deposit.

Applicant is also required to submit a completed Carnival Financial Report due no later
than ten days after the conclusion of the carnival activity.

Fiscal Impact:

The following summarizes the average City expenses incurred from conducting a
carnival:

  Trash bin setup and removal  $  66
  Civic Center lawn restoration  $ 1,048
  Total City Carnival Expenses (per occurrence)  $ 1,114

In the past, the City has absorbed the costs outlined above. In addition, while policy
requires a security deposit, that deposit has been waived previously for the event. While
the City waives the security deposit fees, the organization is still held responsible for all
incidentals. The organization indicates they will be responsible for any damage to
sprinklers or facilities, and their history indicates they have responsibly managed previous
carnivals and the City’s facilities.

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends City Council approve the carnival requested by the Norwalk Float
Foundation for the dates of Thursday, February 13 through Sunday, February 16, 2020
and waive the security deposit and fees as requested consistent with past practice.

Attachments:

Norwalk Float Foundation Request Letter
